driving_question: The "incommunicability axiom" ("You are the Athanor and no one can tell you how to turn the lead into gold") paired with "hylics cannot see" reads the core measurement gap of techgnosis as ONTOLOGICAL. Does any book in the library actually hand over the lead-to-gold procedure, or do they all just describe the gap?
book: Technic and Magic: The Reconstruction of Reality (Federico Campagna)
best_collision: the /x/ axiom says the transformation cannot be transmitted (no one can tell you), but Campagna p.16 says the crisis IS the transmission: the substitution between realities is now frozen in full view, so the gap between worlds is no longer a secret backstage but the visible state of the stage - the incommunicable became communicable precisely by becoming the permanent, witnessed, frozen substitution
quote: What if, along the chain of catastrophes leading from one form of reality to the next, at some point the substitution was frozen at its most disconcerting moment, in full view? How could the characters keep acting, and what in the world could save them from paralysis, if the world (and not just their world) had disintegrated? — p.16
mutation_note: The board keeps insisting the gap is incommunicable: no one can tell you how to turn the lead into gold. Campagna, writing in 2018 from a Sicilian puppet theatre, answers from the opposite side: the curtain never closes anymore. The swap between realities is now public, the void behind the background is in full view, and the puppeteer is gone. The incommunicable didn't stay hidden - it became the visible, permanent, frozen state everyone is forced to watch. The lead-to-gold procedure is not a secret that will be revealed; it is the act of keeping the puppets moving on a stage whose world has visibly disintegrated. The gap was never a wall. It was the backdrop, mid-swap, with the lights left on.
